title: Why Octopuses Have Three Hearts
description:
Octopuses run on three hearts and blue blood — and two of those hearts stop beating every time they swim. Here's why evolution built them this way.

#shorts #sciencefacts #octopus

scenes.text: An octopus has three hearts. And when it swims, one of them actually stops beating.
Two of the hearts pump blood to the gills, and one pumps it to the rest of the body.
That third heart is so inefficient at circulating blood during swimming that octopuses get tired fast, and mostly prefer crawling.
Their blood is also blue, not red, because it uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen.
That copper-based blood works better in cold, low-oxygen water, exactly where a lot of octopuses live.
Three hearts, blue blood, and nine brains total. The ocean did not hold back on this one.
